starting_points.name: Initialize the Go module
starting_points.when: A new Go service has no go.mod; preserve an existing module rather than reinitializing it.
steps: Install the project-selected Go toolchain; choose an empty local source directory outside synced storage.
Replace /path/to/workspace and example.com/project with the real local path and module import path; create project once, then enter it.
Initialize metadata, then implement the net/http service and its tests; the standard library does not provide an application scaffold generator.

commands.purpose: Create go.mod using the real module path.

notes: There is no universal Go net/http service generator in this profile. Routing, configuration validation, graceful shutdown and tests remain application work.

follow_up_generators.name: sqlc query code
follow_up_generators.when: Only when sqlc is selected and schema, annotated queries and sqlc.yaml/sqlc.json have been written.

commands.purpose: Generate typed query access from owned SQL inputs.

notes: Install and record a selected sqlc release first. Configure pgx/v5 output for this profile. Regenerate after schema/query changes; this command does not create migrations or the HTTP application.

follow_up_generators.name: goose SQL migration
follow_up_generators.when: Only when goose owns migrations for this database.

commands.purpose: Create a timestamped migration to edit and review.

notes: Install and record a selected goose release first. Keep one migration owner. Write and test migration SQL using a disposable PostgreSQL database before deployment.

follow_up_generators.name: templ component code
follow_up_generators.when: Only when the optional templ UI has been selected and .templ source exists.

commands.purpose: Generate Go component code from .templ sources.

notes: Match the selected CLI and module versions; preserve editable .templ inputs and the chosen generated-code policy.

follow_up_generators.name: GoReleaser configuration
follow_up_generators.when: Only when GoReleaser is selected for this application and no release configuration exists.
notes: Install and record the project-selected GoReleaser release first. Review build entry points, targets, hooks and publishing settings; generation does not authorize a release.

preserve: Preserve go.mod and go.sum when generated by dependency resolution; record the Go version and resolved generator versions.
go mod init creates module metadata, not source files, tests, a service structure or .gitignore. Add project-specific ignores, including OS metadata, without claiming they came from Go.
Keep generator-created files as the baseline; document deliberate changes and do not replace standard defaults with a handwritten approximation.
Preserve SQL migrations, sqlc configuration, query sources and the agreed generated-code policy.
verification: In the actual project, record generator versions and commands, then compare its initial files with a fresh output from the same versions and options.
After source exists, run gofmt -l ., go test ./..., go vet ./... and go build ./... from the module root; a bare go.mod is not a runnable application.

In a disposable copy, check candidate staging includes source and required manifests but excludes binaries, caches, local credentials and .DS_Store; inspect git add --dry-run -A before changing a real index.
For selected tools, regenerate sqlc/templ and inspect changes; validate migrations against a disposable database.

sources.title: Go modules reference: go mod init

integration_steps: Resolve and record the selected Go/tool versions and dependencies; add pgx/v5 for PostgreSQL and River only when durable jobs are required.
After module initialization, implement the service entry point and application packages with typed settings, explicit http.Server limits, health/readiness and graceful shutdown.

When sqlc and goose are selected, use the follow-up generator instructions; write migrations, annotated queries and sqlc configuration, then generate typed query access. Keep database credentials in environment/secrets.
With GOOSE_DRIVER=postgres and GOOSE_DBSTRING pointing only to a disposable database, run goose -dir migrations up. Add HTTP, real-database, business transaction and selected River enqueue tests.

Add and review the chosen release configuration, pin tools and preserve go.mod/go.sum; document build, deployment and rollback. Qualify target runtime/cgo requirements. These application steps have not been executed.
